newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE VOLUME UP IN NEW FOREIGN INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE VOLUME UP IN NEW FOREIGN INTEREST.

text.p: Fresh foreign interest in Romanian equities after the government approved portfolio investment rules boosted volumes and turnover on the Bucharest stock exchange on Thursday.
"There was positive perception of the government's move and foreigners have increased their presence," a broker said.
Volume climbed to 3.2 million shares from 2.8 million and turnover rose to 10.8 billion lei from 8.7 billion.
The average prices of 15 stocks went up, 13 fell and three were flat. Seven had no trade and three were suspended.
The unofficial VAB index, computed by market capitalisation and average prices, rose by 2.4 percent from Wednesday. The other independent index, the BIG, was unavailable.
The new portfolio rules, announced on Wednesday, set a four percent tax on capital gains repatriation.
Traders said they expected foreign interest to rise over the next few sessions, pushing volumes higher.
The bourse issued the results of its Thursday session with delay due to what it called irregularities during trading.

Brokers said the exchange had failed to inform them in time of a share split at car parts maker Apsa , which lowered the nominal value of its shares to 1,000 lei each from 25,000 after a mass selloff oversubscription.
A new market price for Apsa should have been set but instead deals were made at the older market price of 8,000 lei. The deals were later annulled.
The first tier was in the focus on Thursday, taking 80 percent of turnover. Five of six high-caps gained on their average prices. Four also closed higher in late trading.
Pharmaceuticals companies Antibiotice and Terapia closed 300 and 150 lei higher at 5,150 and 6,400.
Chemical plant Oltchim and Azomures fertiliser maker closed stronger under buying pressure, traders said. Oltchim gained 300 lei to end at 2,850 and Azomures gained 250 lei to close at 3,300.

Sofert fertiliser maker and refrigerator maker Arctic lost 11,000 and 350 lei respectively to close at 64,000 and 3,400. Traders explained the drops by saying Arctic was new to the market and Sofert was too expensive.
Policolor dye maker stayed in the limelight on the second tier with 1.7 billion lei in turnover and a closing price 150 lei firmer at 5,500.
